prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
UKIP Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core stance
- Leave the EU to regain sovereignty, control borders, laws and trade; hold an immediate in/out referendum (British citizens only), prefer Article 50 exit. Seek a bespoke UK–EU free-trade deal and wider global FTAs; maintain cooperation on security, health and science agencies. Establish a Post‑EU Secretariat to unwind EU law.

Public finances and tax
- Fund plans by: saving £9bn net EU contributions; cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI; scrapping HS2; replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs‑based system; ending “health tourism”; and cutting government/quangos.
- Tax: raise personal allowance to at least £13,000 (no income tax on minimum wage); introduce a 30% band between £43.5k–£55k; raise the 40% threshold to £55k; abolish inheritance tax; increase transferable allowance for married/civil partners; cut small business rates (20% relief under £50k rateable value). Close multinational avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.

NHS and social care
- Extra £12bn over five years; 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GP pilots in A&E; £1.5bn for mental health/dementia; free hospital parking; end PFI; replace CQC/Monitor with elected county health boards; scrap EU Clinical Trials and Working Time directives; exclude NHS from TTIP. Social care: restore funding to 2010 levels (+£1.2bn/yr), integrate with NHS, dignity code, abolish 15‑minute visits, increase Carer’s Allowance by £572/yr; explore shale-funded sovereign wealth fund for care cap.

Immigration and borders
- End EU free movement; Australian-style points system; five‑year moratorium on unskilled immigration; +2,500 Border Agency staff; strict visas; five years’ tax/NI before access to benefits and most NHS care; no amnesty for illegal migrants; deport foreign criminals; revoke citizenship for terrorists by law change. EU citizens resident at referendum may remain and apply for citizenship after five years.

Welfare, pensions, families
- Tighter benefit cap and fraud action; scrap bedroom tax; pay Housing Benefit to under‑25s; reform disability assessments via GPs/specialists; fund 800 advisers in foodbanks. Flexible state pension window; expand pensions guidance; criminalise pension cold‑calling; restore lifelong war widows’ pensions. Childcare: deregulate to expand places and cut costs; statutory wrap‑around care (8am–6pm).

Education and skills
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; expand grammar and vocational/technical schools with later transfer tests; apprenticeships can replace four non‑core GCSEs; rework GCSE tiers; keep AS as standalone; first‑aid in PSHE; reverse special-school closures; refocus Ofsted. Waive tuition fees for UK STEMM/Medicine students who work and pay tax in UK for five years.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield (register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief up to £250k); bring empty homes back; build 1m on brownfield by 2025; protect green belt; local referendums on large schemes; “local connection” priority for social housing; restrict Right to Buy/Help to Buy to British citizens (armed forces exception for non‑British on RTB). Homelessness register.

Transport and energy
- Scrap HS2; consider Manston airport; limit speed cameras to safety; oppose road pricing/eCall; end most tolls; double HGV levy for foreign trucks; VED exemption for 25+‑year vehicles. Repeal Climate Change Act; end wind/solar subsidies and green levies/ETS; back hydro, nuclear, gas, shale (with safeguards and sovereign wealth fund), and coal (new efficient plants, end EU combustion directives); cut prepayment penalties.

Jobs, business and trade
- Prioritise British workers; curb EURES/relocation grants; enforce minimum wage; regulate zero‑hours abuses. Help SMEs: rate relief, crackdown on late payments (HMRC fines), pilot trade credit insurance, 30‑minute free town‑centre parking, cut EU red tape, open public contracts.

Farming, fishing, heritage
- New Single Farm Payment (£80/acre, capped), support dairy/sheep, tougher animal welfare, ban live exports, enable small abattoirs. Leave CFP; UK 12‑mile and 200‑mile EEZ; rebuild stocks; favour under‑10m fleet; protect anglers. Create Heritage/Tourism minister; remove VAT on listed‑building repairs; “seaside town status”; save pubs (micro-brewery tax breaks, optional ventilated smoking rooms, oppose alcohol minimum pricing, reverse tobacco plain packs).

Crime, justice, defence, culture
- 6,000 extra posts across police, prisons and borders; review constabulary structure/PCCs; invest in tech; decriminalise TV licence non‑payment. Leave ECHR jurisdiction; repeal HRA; UK Bill of Rights; end European Arrest Warrant. Defence: spend ≥2% GDP (rising by up to £4bn by 2020), retain Trident, restore capabilities, carriers in service, review F‑35, create Director of National Intelligence, oppose EU army; no income tax on active service. Promote British culture, integration and English language; add St George’s and St David’s Day bank holidays.

Overseas aid
- Cut to 0.2% of GNI; focus on emergencies, vaccinations, clean water/sanitation; merge DFID into FCO; “trade not aid,” prefer UK providers.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core approach
- Budget Responsibility Lock: cut the deficit every year; get debt falling and a current budget surplus ASAP; no new spending paid for by extra borrowing; OBR to audit party manifestos.

Tax and public finances
- Restore 50p top rate over £150k; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by ending the Marriage Allowance.
- No rises in basic/higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; no VAT extension to essentials.
- Abolish non-dom status; clamp down on avoidance/evasion; review HMRC culture.

Economy, industry and infrastructure
- National Infrastructure Commission; support HS2 and northern rail, strategic roads, cycling; swift airport-capacity decision.
- Long-term science funding; leadership in low-carbon tech; decarbonise power by 2030; empower Green Investment Bank; create an Energy Security Board.
- British Investment Bank and regional banks; boost high-street banking competition; payday lender levy.
- Support small firms: cut then freeze business rates; tackle late payment.
- Digital: universal affordable high-speed broadband and wider mobile coverage.
- Corporate governance reforms: empower long-term investors; curb short-termism; employee voice on pay.
- Royal Mail: retain 30% public stake; staff-led trust for employee shares.

Work, pay and opportunities
- Raise National Minimum Wage to >£8/hour by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and “Make Work Pay” tax rebates.
- Ban exploitative zero-hours contracts; close agency-worker loopholes; scrap employment tribunal fees system.
- Youth/jobs: compulsory Jobs Guarantee (bank bonus tax-funded); guarantee an apprenticeship for qualified school leavers; expand public-sector apprenticeships; create Technical Degrees; reduce tuition fees to £6,000; Youth Allowance tied to training; curb unpaid internships.

Consumer markets and transport
- Freeze energy bills until 2017; reform market (separate generation/supply, open exchange, tougher watchdog); 1m interest-free efficiency loans; PRS minimum energy standards.
- Water affordability scheme; stronger regulation.
- Rail reform: allow a public operator; fare freeze for a year then caps; legal right to cheapest ticket; devolve bus powers and integrate local transport.

NHS and care
- Fund 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives (mansion tax, tobacco levy, anti-avoidance).
- 48-hour GP appointments; one-week cancer tests and a Cancer Treatments Fund.
- Repeal Health and Social Care Act; NHS preferred provider; cap private profits; integrate physical, mental and social care; mental health parity with 28-day access to talking therapies.
- Public health: limits on sugar/salt/fat in foods marketed to children.
- End 15-minute care visits; recruit 5,000 home-care workers; stronger support for carers.

Education and children
- Protect entire education budget (early years to post-16).
- Technical Baccalaureate; Institutes of Technical Education; English/Maths to 18; independent careers advice.
- All teachers qualified; Master Teacher status; School Leadership Institute.
- Local Directors of School Standards; end Free Schools programme; cap infant classes at 30; require private-school partnerships with state schools.
- Compulsory, age-appropriate sex and relationships education; character and anti-bullying programmes.

Families, housing and welfare
- Free childcare 25 hours for 3–4s (working parents); wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave to 4 weeks and raise pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first dibs for local first-time buyers; “use it or lose it” on land; garden cities; back small builders and public building.
- Private renting: three-year tenancies as standard; ceiling on excessive rent rises; ban letting fees; landlord register.
- Abolish the Bedroom Tax; keep household benefit cap (review locally); tailored back-to-work support; pause/review Universal Credit; reform Work Capability Assessment; specialist disability employment support; protect pension triple lock; restrict Winter Fuel Payments for richest 5%.

Immigration, policing and justice
- 1,000 extra border staff; exit checks; tighter short-term study visas; retain non-EU worker cap; two-year wait for benefits; English requirement for public-facing roles.
- Ban undercutting by agencies; extend Gangmasters Authority remit; humane asylum (end indefinite detention for vulnerable groups).
- Safeguard 10,000 police officers by abolishing PCCs, sharing services; Local Policing Commitment; replace IPCC; Victims’ Law; tougher action on domestic abuse; ban “legal highs”.
- Stronger counter-extremism (controls on dangerous suspects, revamped Prevent, de-radicalisation for returnees); zero-tolerance of hate crime.

Devolution, rights and media
- Constitutional Convention; replace House of Lords with an elected Senate of the Nations and Regions.
- English Devolution Act: £30bn to city/county regions; integrate local transport; retain growth business rates; local Public Accounts Committees.
- Implement further powers for Scotland and Wales; fair funding for Wales; support NI progress.
- Votes at 16; fix voter registration; cap party donations; statutory lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships/consultancies.
- Protect Human Rights Act; extend FOI to major private providers of public services; gender pay-gap reporting; race equality strategy; strengthen LGBT rights; media plurality; implement Leveson; keep BBC strong and Channel 4 public.

Europe, defence, climate and development
- Remain in and reform the EU (single market completion, budget discipline, worker rights); “referendum lock” on any power transfers.
- NATO commitment; cautious, legal, multilateral approach to interventions; two-state solution for Israel/Palestine.
- Strategic Defence and Security Review; strengthen Armed Forces Covenant; Veterans’ Register; bolster cyber security; maintain independent nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Lead on climate: push for Paris deal, net zero global emissions in the second half of the century.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; focus on poorest, women and children; create Centre for Universal Health Coverage; strengthen tax transparency and anti-corruption.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_F aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_D" | "TEXT_F"
}
